fields.subnational_unit: Orinoquía (llanos orientales), department of Casanare; community survey in rural Aguazul, Casanare
fields.sample_size: 200 rural drinking-water/sanitation projects collected from the regional environmental authority, the governorate and the municipalities (Table 2 lists 12, 66 and 134, which sum to 212, not 200); 42 formulated-and-executed projects selected for the 14-variable review; community survey of 20 residents of rural Aguazul, Casanare (sampling not described beyond 'defined statistically by descriptive analysis')
fields.effect_measure: descriptive percentage of the 42 reviewed projects that took each of 14 variables into account (Table 4) and percentage yes/no answers of 20 surveyed residents (Table 5); no inferential statistics
fields.effect_estimate: Share of the 42 projects that took each variable into account (Table 4): citizen participation 14.3%; technological change, community type and sectorisation 0%; geographic information system 66.6%; sanitary assessment by census 67% (by the RAS 2000 technical regulation 100%); socioeconomic evaluation 83.3%; coverage 83.3%; administration 78.6%; legal analysis 99%; governability, public-private participation, prioritisation/maintenance and technological appropriation 100%. The author concludes that the projects tend to meet legal minimums but not non-mandatory parameters that matter to communities, and that participation is not a mandatory item in project formulation. Survey of 20 residents (Table 5, pairings read in order from the converted text): 10% say projects were socialised before formulation, 0% were asked about their needs, 15% worked on a design, 20% say projects meet the whole community's needs, 10% are informed of new projects, 5% report training before handover, 30% say the community is linked to execution; 100% say communities should be included and that primary data should be collected first. Respondents who said they were consulted were landowners or Community Action Board presidents.
fields.section: Full text (Spanish, 7 pages): Materials and methods 2.1-2.3.5; Results (Tables 3-5, Figs. 3-5); Discussion; Conclusions; Recommendations

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a descriptive document review of 42 rural water/sanitation projects in the Colombian llanos (compliance percentages per variable) plus a 20-person community survey; read in full text 2026-10-04. Qualitative/descriptive, no inferential statistics.
pdf_note: DYNA 85(204):289-295, 7 pages, Spanish with English abstract (Drive file S270_Rivera_Contreras_2018...pdf) read in full; figures and the converted layout of Tables 1, 2 and 5 are partly scrambled, so the Table 5 pairings were read in order and the project counts of Table 2 do not sum to the 200 in the abstract
notes: Supplies the numeric compliance and survey results that the abstract-only extraction left out; the paper's Table 2 (12+66+134=212) disagrees with its abstract (200 collected).
